question_stem:
Polonium-211 (^{211}_{84}Po) is radioactive and decays by alpha emission to form a stable isotope of lead (Pb).
The alpha particle is emitted with kinetic energy 7.45 MeV.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Complete the equation for the decay of Polonium-211.
$$^{211}_{84}\text{Po} \rightarrow \text{................... Pb} + \text{................... }\alpha$$

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
Use Fig. 9.1 to determine the decay constant $\lambda$ of Polonium-211.
$$\lambda = \text{...................................................... s}^{-1}$$

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Calculate the activity at time $t = 0$ of the sample of Polonium-211.
$$\text{activity} = \text{...................................................... Bq}$$

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: On Fig. 9.1, sketch a line to show the variation with $t$ of the number of Lead nuclei in the sample.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
Calculate the total energy, in J, released in the decay of $8.8 \times 10^{12}$ nuclei of Polonium-211.
$$\text{energy} = \text{...................................................... J}$$

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why the total mass of the lead nucleus and the alpha particle is less than the initial mass of the polonium nucleus.
